title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

description:
Figure Drawing Group in Davis 
Wednesday, October 14, 6:30-9 PM 
$15 Members, $22 Non-Members | Limited to 10 participants

We hold self-guided figure drawing sessions with a nude model every 2nd & 4th Wednesday of the month, from 6:30–9 PM. This group is for both experienced artists and amateurs to have an opportunity to draw from the nude model. If you have never drawn from a live model before and would like to join us, you are very welcome! People of all skill levels, ages 18 and up, are welcome and encouraged to join. 
  
This is not a class, and no instruction is provided. The atmosphere is relaxed and non-competitive. Bring your own art materials, and we’ll provide a comfortable place to sketch or paint live models in our upstairs classroom space. Participants will work independently through a warm up with shorter poses and longer, twenty-minute poses. A staff member will be on-site to facilitate the group and to answer questions.

title: Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill
location: Pence Gallery, 212 D Street, Davis, CA 95616
description:
Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill at Pence Gallery in Davis 
Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 
Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) 
Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free) 
  
Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout the duration of the show.  
  
Sponsored by the Pence Community Curatorial Fund. 
  
Image: Gioia Fonda, “Holding It Together”

title: Bat Week Screening of “The Invisible Mammal” and Davis Premiere
location: Davis Veterans Memorial Theater, 277 E. 14th Street, Davis CA, Davis, 95616, United States
description:
Join cast, crew and our screening partners on Thursday, October 15, 2026 for a special Bat Week event: the Davis, CA Premiere of The Invisible Mammal, the award-winning feature documentary about bat conservation.
Against the backdrop of the sixth mass extinction, an all-woman team of biologists set out to save bats from a deadly fungal disease. Meet director Kristin Tièche and castmember Corky Quirk and her ambassador bats!

title: Artist Talk with Mercy Hawkins
location: Pence Gallery, 212 D Street, Davis, CA 95616
description:
Artist Talk with Mercy Hawkins in Davis 
Saturday, October 17, 2-3:30 PM (Free) 
  
Mercy Hawkins will speak about the development and trajectory of several bodies of recent work, including its connection to craft. She will also explore the intersection of painting and music.  
  
Waltz of Life & Limb pairs Hawkins’ recent sculptural paintings with her vibrant, large-scale watercolors on paper. Her imagery evokes seed pods, flower buds, or microscopic creatures, immersing the viewer in an all-encompassing perception of nature. The exhibit is on display at the Pence Gallery from October 3 – November 6, 2026.

title: Imagining America National Gathering
description:
Join over 500 participants from the IA network and the University of California, Davis and Yolo Bioregion community (a geographic and cultural area that includes the cities of Davis, Woodland, Winters, West Sacramento, and surrounding areas) to engage in deep learning, collaboration, and transformative creativity on the theme of Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times. We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. 
Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times calls us to re-story and honor the places, knowledges, relationships, and ecologies that have been made broken through centuries of violence and abandonment, and the current intensifying fear and repression. We know that our communities are tired, and we know that being together revives our collective spirit, giving us the strength and inspiration we need in troubled times. In this moment of upheaval, the 2026 IA National Gathering draws participants to Davis, CA in the spirit of mending the roots of our connections, and to “awaken,” as Buddhist monk and activist Thích Nhất Hạnh teaches, “from the illusion of our separateness.”

title: Voting from Different Perspectives: Studying Elections across Disciplines
location: Virtual
description:

This panel brings together faculty from across UC Davis and UC Davis Health discuss their research on voting and elections within and between different disciplines as well as national and international contexts. The panel aims to share research, advance research literacy, and explore scholarly boundaries of expertise as well as areas for cross-pollination. 
Panelists will include: 

Vikram D. Amar, Daniel J. Dykstra Distinguished Professor of Law
Ruth Shim, Director of Cultural Psychiatry and Luke & Grace Kim Professor in Cultural Psychiatry, Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
Lauren Young, Associate Professor and Director of Graduate Studies, Political Science
Megan Macklin (moderator), Director of Campus Climate and Inclusion Initiatives, Office of Campus and Community Relations/Inclusive Excellence

You must register in advance for this event.

title: Figure Drawing Group

description:
Figure Drawing Group in Davis 
Wednesday, October 28, 6:30-9 PM 
$15 Members, $22 Non-Members | Limited to 10 participants

We hold self-guided figure drawing sessions with a nude model every 2nd & 4th Wednesday of the month, from 6:30–9 PM. This group is for both experienced artists and amateurs to have an opportunity to draw from the nude model. If you have never drawn from a live model before and would like to join us, you are very welcome! People of all skill levels, ages 18 and up, are welcome and encouraged to join.

title: International Festival Davis
location: International House Davis, 10 College Park, Davis, 95616, United States
description:
Join us on November 7 at International House Davis for I-Fest 2026, our International Festival Davis! 
For one day, we open our doors wide to celebrate and uplift the many cultures and people who make our region so vibrant. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. 
I-Fest is a celebration, but your participation also supports the work I-House does all year long: welcoming newcomers, supporting English learners, and helping people from around the world find connection and community in Davis. At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever. Come celebrate cultures, meet new people, share in the joy, and experience what makes our community so special. 
For one day, I-House is your house. Come be part of it.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.
